name: Dumpu-Watiwa
confidence_why: one confirmed first-hand source; 9 other works read were silent
catalog_citation: Z'graggen, Johannes A. 1980. A comparative word list of the Rai Coast languages, Madang Province, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics D-30. Canberra: Research School of Pacific Studies, Australian National University.
catalog_locator: p. 172, Notes, entry (PDF page 188 of the ANU open-access scan; page image (PDF p. 188 agrees)
catalog_quote: Claassen and McElhanon (1970:60) classify Dumpu or Watiwa as a member of the Kabenau Family. The present writer links Dumpu with the Evapia Family, but additional data collected by the present writer in June 1975 appear to be more in support of a link with the Kabenau Family. The language name Watiwa was then also confirmed. It may be noted that the Dumpu-Watiwa language is tonal.

new_statements.rule_in_words: No rule for word stress is given. The only prosodic statement in print is Z'graggen's one-line remark, based on his own June 1975 field data, that Dumpu-Watiwa is a tone language; nothing is said about stress, and the wordlist forms (transcribed 'semiphonemically', p.viii) carry no tone or stress marks.
new_statements.domain_note: Remark made in the classificatory notes of a comparative wordlist; no phonological analysis, no examples of tonal contrast, no statement about word-level vs phrase-level prosody.
new_statements.identity_note: The source calls the language 'Dumpu' or 'Dumpu-Watiwa' (wordlist language B5, Kabenau/Evapia Rai Coast); Dumpu is a village name, Watiwa the speakers' own name (ISO CR 2010-028). Same languoid as dump1243 [wtf]; no dialects distinguished anywhere.

The present writer links Dumpu with the Evapia Family, but additional data collected by the present writer in June 1975 appear to be more in support of a link with the Kabenau Family. sources.locator: p. 172 (Notes, note 3); PDF page 188 of the ANU scan
sources.note: Nothing about stress. Note 3 on p.172 (pdf p.188) states 'It may be noted that the Dumpu-Watiwa language is tonal.' The wordlist itself is 'semiphonemic' (p.viii) and the Dumpu (B5) forms carry no tone or stress marks (checked p.16 eye/mouth and pronoun table); p.viii lists Dumpu sound fluctuations p~f, l~r only.
No descriptive references; classification refs Claassen & McElhanon 1970:49 and Z'graggen 1980. Alt names Watiwa, Watifa.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Watiwa is treated only in para 3.3.5 (p.60): 250 speakers in Dumpu, Abikal, Bembei; 12-24% cognates with Kabenau, 15-18% with Evapia, 'may prove to be a language isolate'. The phonology section 6.1 covers Yaganon, Suroi, Evapia, Rawa, Yupna, Uruwa, Wantoat only, not Watiwa; no stress/tone remarks anywhere.
